minutes.headline: Parks Commission left field fees unchanged until the FY28 maintenance contract is known, and tabled Wallace Park lights.
minutes.summary: The commission voted to partner with the LBA on a May 2027 spring vendor fair, reviewed a spreadsheet of FY26 field costs, and discussed field usage fees without changing them. It also took up the lack of a written agreement with the schools for facility use, the rec director's funding, and proposed Wallace Park lights. It approved overdue April minutes and tabled the lights until the revolving fund balance is confirmed.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; the one member of the public present declined to speak.
A resident and property owner said the facilities contract is already funded by property taxes, questioned recouping costs from leagues, and said they had rarely seen the irrigation running.

votes.motion: Partner with the LBA for the spring vendor fair on May 22, 2027, rain date May 23, 2027, with no guarantees of support.
Approve the April minutes, which had never been approved.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member totalled the FY26 invoices and found them close to the landscape contract, though individual field lines differed. About two thousand of the total was Memorial Veterans Park.
Water is about nine thousand a year for Marshall Park, inflated by a tampered irrigation timer. A new bill was thought too high. Locks and rain shut-offs are being added.

budget_items.topic: Eversource-type electric bills offset by solar credits
budget_items.what_was_said: Field electric bills are tiny because of town solar credits. Wallace pays a flat meter fee because it uses no power.

budget_items.topic: Youth baseball user fees against cost of maintaining its fields
budget_items.what_was_said: Baseball pays a per-player fee that totals far less than the infield maintenance contract lines for its fields.
Fees started at zero, then ten, and were raised to twenty per resident player in November 2020. Non-residents pay thirty.

budget_items.topic: Travel program (Brigade) paying resident/non-resident per-player rate
budget_items.what_was_said: A for-profit travel program pays the youth per-player rate, a few hundred in total, despite charging families far more.

budget_items.topic: Possible seasonal fee for concession stand use
budget_items.what_was_said: A member suggested a seasonal fee for the concession stand to fund its upkeep.

budget_items.topic: Parks revolving fund balance and cost of Wallace lights
budget_items.what_was_said: Lights were quoted at a low amount, but the fund shows limited available budget and the rec director's salary is paid from it. Members want the balance confirmed before voting.
The commission is covering the rec director's salary on a trial run and may not afford a second year from its own budget.

decisions.decision: No change to field user fees this year; revisit after the FY28 maintenance contract costs are known.
Aim for a consensus on fees by the January meeting, with a fee discussion in December and a vote in January.
Members asked to think about renaming and splitting user categories and bring proposed per-player or hourly rates to the next meeting.
Two members will meet with town staff or the town manager to craft a facilities agreement with the schools before approaching the superintendent's office.
Wallace Park lights tabled until the revolving fund balance after salary is confirmed with the town.
Next meeting to be held in early December rather than the Wednesday before Thanksgiving.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission made no change to field user fees this year and will revisit them once the FY28 maintenance contract costs are known.
Wallace Park lights were tabled until the town confirms the revolving fund balance after the rec director's salary is paid from it.
The commission voted to partner with the LBA on a spring vendor fair on May 22, 2027; the minutes record the vote tally as not audible.
Members aim to reach a consensus on fees by January, with a discussion in December and a vote in January.
Two members will meet town staff or the town manager to draft a facilities agreement with the schools before approaching the superintendent's office.

why_it_matters: Youth leagues' per-player fees stay as they are for now, while the minutes show baseball fees totalling far less than the infield maintenance contract lines for its fields, so the question of who pays for field upkeep stays open into the winter.
The rec director's salary is paid from the same parks revolving fund that would pay for Wallace Park lights, so a new park amenity competes with a staff position for one pot of money.
Schools and town fields are used without a written agreement, so who may use them and who pays for upkeep rests on nothing in writing until one is drafted.
watch_next: A fee discussion at the December meeting, held in early December rather than the week before Thanksgiving, and a fee vote in January.
The town's confirmation of the parks revolving fund balance, which the commission needs before it takes up Wallace Park lights again.
